title: Relative torsor representatives and the two boundary signs
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $j:W=T\setminus Z\hookrightarrow T$ its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $G$ be an abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and let $(P,s)$ be a $G$-torsor with a specified section on $W$ [def-amb-torsor-with-section]. Use the raw lifting-cocycle class $\alpha(P,s)$, the negative of the Ext-normalized canonical relative class of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology]. Its negative forgetful image is the torsor $H^1$ class [lem-amb-relative-torsor-forget-normalization]. Use the signed relative complex $C_G^q=I_G^q(T)\oplus I_G^{q-1}(W)$ with differential $D(a,b)=(da,\operatorname{res}(a)-db)$ [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology]. Form the canonical torsor extension $0\to G\to E_P\to\mathbf Z_T\to0$ of [lem-sc-torsor-h1, def-sc-torsor-extension-presentation]. For any nonnegative injective resolution $G\to I_G^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and any extension $h:E_P\to I_G^0$ of its augmentation, let $a\in I_G^1(T)$ be obtained by factoring $dh$ through $\mathbf Z_T$ and evaluating at $1$, and let $b=h(s)\in I_G^0(W)$. Then $\alpha(P,s)$ is represented by $(a,b)$ in this signed cone, independently of $h$ and of the resolution. In particular, for any $g\in G(W)$ the class $\alpha_g$ of the trivial torsor $G$ with specified section $g$ is represented by $(0,g)$, with $g$ inserted in $I_G^0(W)$, and $\alpha_g=-\partial_G^0(g)$, where $\partial_G^q:H^q(W,G)\to H^{q+1}(T,W;G)$ is the localization boundary represented on this cone by $b\mapsto(0,-b)$. More generally, let $0\to G_1\to G_2\to G_3\to0$ be any short exact sequence of abelian etale sheaves, let $g\in G_3(W)$, and let $\delta_W:H^0(W,G_3)\to H^1(W,G_1)$ and $\delta_{T,W}:H^1(T,W;G_3)\to H^2(T,W;G_1)$ be the ordinary and relative connecting maps. With $\alpha_g$ the relative class of $(G_3,g)$, one has $\delta_{T,W}(\alpha_g)=\partial_{G_1}^1(\delta_W(g))$. In degreewise split injective resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses], a lift $r\in I_2^0(W)$ of the cocycle $g$ gives $dr\in I_1^1(W)$ and the two classes in this equality are both represented by $(0,-dr)$. All these identifications are natural under etale restriction of the pair and morphisms of short exact coefficient sequences.

proof.text: Transport a section cycle through the shift short-complex isomorphism, then apply the shifted cone inclusion. Its signed first coordinate is zero and its signed second coordinate is minus the original section. Homology quotient naturality proves the localization assertion in every degree. The zero lifting torsor identifies the trivial pair with (0,g); uniqueness of signed coordinates gives its class as minus this localization boundary.

proof.text: Evaluate each specified splitting and extend by zero; the extended rows remain split in nonnegative degrees and are zero in negative degrees. Thus the open section sequence is short exact. Lift the augmented g to r using the split row in degree zero. Its derivative maps to zero, so exactness of the split degree-one row gives c with a(c)=dr. Mathlib ShortExact.delta_apply on the open sequence identifies the ordinary boundary with [c]. In the relative sequence the signed cochain (0,r) maps to (0,g) and has derivative (0,-dr); the same concrete boundary formula yields the representative (0,-c). This agrees with the localization representative, so coordinate uniqueness proves the double-boundary identity. Repeat this computation for every allowed r.

old_proof.text: Write $A=I_G(T)$, $B=I_G(W)$ and $r:A\to B$ for restriction. The relative definition computes the derived fibre of $r$. With the cone and shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its signed model is $C^q=A^q\oplus B^{q-1}$, $D(a,b)=(da,ra-db)$; this is the functor in [lem-amb-signed-fibre-triangulated]. In degree one the cycle equations are $da=0$, $ra=db$, and the boundaries are $D(x)=(dx,rx)$ because the resolution has no negative terms. To fix the localization sign, the ordinary cone is $\operatorname{Cone}(r)^q=B^q\oplus A^{q+1}$ with differential $(db+ra,-da)$ and boundary $-p$. The chain isomorphism $C[1]\to\operatorname{Cone}(r)$ is $(a,b)\mapsto(-b,a)$. The cone inclusion $b\mapsto(b,0)$ therefore becomes $b\mapsto(0,-b)$ in $C[1]$. This is exactly the localization boundary used in the statement, in every degree.

Let $\epsilon:G\hookrightarrow I_G^0$ be the augmentation and write $\iota:G\hookrightarrow E_P$, $p:E_P\to\mathbf Z_T$ and $\jmath:P\to E_P$ for the presentation maps. The canonical short exact extension is supplied by [lem-sc-torsor-h1], and [def-sc-torsor-extension-presentation] gives $\jmath(g+t)=\iota(g)+\jmath(t)$ and $p\jmath(t)=1$. Injectivity in [def-sp-injective-resolutions] extends $\epsilon$ along $\iota$ to $h$. Since $dh\iota=d\epsilon=0$, exactness of the extension factors $dh$ uniquely as $\bar a p$. Since $p$ is epi and $d^2h=0$, $d\bar a=0$. Set $a=\bar a(1)$ and $b=h\jmath(s)$. The equation $p\jmath(s)=1$ gives $db=ra$, so $(a,b)$ is a relative cycle by step 1.

old_proof.text: Here is the relative-class identification, including the specified section. For a cycle $(a,b)$ let $P_a(U)=\{t\in I_G^0(U):dt=a|_U\}$. In the present case the natural map $P\to P_a$ is $t\mapsto h\jmath(t)$ and is $G$-equivariant. On any etale object admitting a section $t_0$ of $P$, every solution $x$ differs from $h\jmath(t_0)$ by a unique section of $G$, because $\ker(d:I_G^0\to I_G^1)=\epsilon(G)$ as sheaves. Thus this map is an isomorphism locally, and its local inverses agree by uniqueness, giving a sheaf isomorphism. It carries $s$ to $b$. This computes the canonical relative refinement [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] of the extension correspondence [lem-sc-torsor-h1]: the lift of $1$ has differential $a$, and its prescribed trivialization on $W$ is the nullhomotopy $b$, whose equation is $db=ra$. These are exactly the two components of a class in the derived fibre, rather than merely an absolute class together with an unspecified lift. Equivalently, the inverse construction sends $(a,b)$ to the solution torsor with specified solution $b$, and the displayed isomorphism recovers $(P,s)$. Translation by $x\in I_G^0(T)$ carries $(P_a,b)$ to $(P_{a+dx},b+rx)$, so this description respects relative boundaries. Consequently $[(a,b)]=\alpha(P,s)$.

old_proof.text: If $h'$ is another extension of $\epsilon$, the difference $h'-h$ kills $G$ and hence factors uniquely as $\bar x p:E_P\to I_G^0$. Put $x=\bar x(1)\in I_G^0(T)$. The definitions give $a'-a=dx$ and $b'-b=rx$, so their representatives differ by the boundary $D(x)$ of step 1. This proves independence of $h$ without choosing any global section of $P$.

old_proof.text: For independence of resolutions, apply [lem-amb-bounded-injective-fibre-descent] with $E=\mathrm{id}$, $A=\Gamma(T,-)$, $B=\Gamma(W,-)$, $F=F'$ the signed-fibre functor of [lem-amb-signed-fibre-triangulated], and $\tau=\mathrm{id}$. The abelian sheaf category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. The descent statement supplies a comparison $u:I_G\to J_G$, unique for this purpose up to homotopy, and the induced canonical map on relative cohomology is $(a,b)\mapsto(u^1a,u^0b)$. Its augmentation compatibility is strict: a homotopy from maps out of $G[0]$ into a nonnegative complex has zero component in degree $-1$. Therefore $u^0h$ is an allowed extension into $J_G^0$, and its representative is precisely $(u^1a,u^0b)$. Step 4 removes the choice of extension on $J_G$. The descent theorem removes the comparison choices. Its hypotheses require only bounded below injectives, which both given resolutions are, and its signed homotopy is $(a,b)\mapsto(Ha,-Hb)$. Hence the claimed class and its representative are independent of the resolution under the canonical identifications.

old_proof.text: For the trivial torsor $P=G$, choose its identity section $0$ on $T$. The natural family $t\mapsto\epsilon(t)$ is equivariant. The universal property of [def-sc-torsor-extension-presentation] gives $h:E_G\to I_G^0$ restricting to $\epsilon$ and satisfying $h\jmath(t)=\epsilon(t)$. Since $d\epsilon=0$, the same universal property (with zero coefficient map and zero family) gives $dh=0$. Thus $a=0$ and, for the specified section $g$ on $W$, $b=\epsilon(g)$. Step 3 gives $\alpha_g=[(0,g)]$. Step 1 gives $\partial_G^0(g)=[(0,-g)]$, so $\alpha_g=-\partial_G^0(g)$. If $g$ extends to $G(T)$, this representative is also $D(g)$ and its class vanishes, as required by translation of the specified trivial torsor.

old_proof.text: For the coefficient sequence take the degreewise split nonnegative injective resolutions of [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses]; the enough-injectives hypothesis is [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Applying sections on $T$ and $W$ preserves these split rows, since a sheaf splitting evaluates to a splitting; taking the two finite direct summands gives a split short exact sequence of signed relative complexes. The relative connecting map is the one in [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology]. Choose a lift $r\in I_2^0(W)$ of the augmented cocycle $g$. The image of $d_2r$ in $I_3^1(W)$ is $d_3g=0$, so there is a unique $c\in I_1^1(W)$ mapping to $d_2r$; it is a cocycle because the degree-two inclusion is injective. The split-complex connecting formula [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-connecting-formula] on $W$ gives $\delta_W(g)=[c]$. The relative cycle $(0,g)$ lifts to $(0,r)$, whose differential is $D_2(0,r)=(0,-d_2r)$. The same connecting formula on the relative complexes gives $\delta_{T,W}(\alpha_g)=[(0,-c)]$. By step 1, $\partial_{G_1}^1([c])=[(0,-c)]$, proving the asserted positive equality. Identifying $I_1$ with its image writes $c=dr$, as in the statement. A different lift $r+\iota(t)$ replaces $c$ by $c+dt$; the relative change $(0,-dt)=D_1(0,t)$ is a boundary.

Finally all formulas commute with etale restriction: [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], clause 5, permits restricting an injective resolution and computes pullback by restricting its sections. Thus $h$, $a$, $b$, $r$ and $c$ restrict to the corresponding data on the new pair. Coefficient maps act componentwise on signed cones by [lem-amb-signed-fibre-triangulated]; in particular $(0,-b)$ maps to $(0,-u b)$. The canonical relative torsor bijection and the relative coefficient connecting maps are natural by the statement of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology]. For a morphism of short exact coefficient sequences, [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] applies to the absolute and relative complex sequences, so the lift-and-differentiate classes in step 7 commute with the induced cohomology maps. This does not require a chosen splitting to be preserved: the connecting map is independent of that choice and is natural for any morphism of short exact complex sequences. Combined with step 5 these statements establish naturality for arbitrary choices of the resolutions used to write the representatives.
